newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan stocks close sharply lower on profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan stocks close sharply lower on profit-taking.

text.p: Taiwan share prices closed sharply lower on Wednesday, ignoring the overnight rise on Wall Street as investors continued to take profits off the local market's previous gains, brokers said.
The weighted index, which had risen briefly on Wall Street's surge, suffered late heavy selling and tumbled by 1.24 percent or 106.78 points to 8,485.66 at the close.
Turnover was an active T$116 billion, but much lighter than the hectic volumes registered during the market's recent bull run.
The market has closed lower for the third consecutive session following a six-session bull run that ended on Saturday.
"Investors did not pay attention to Wall Street. They are simply not confident that the market has further room to rise," said Chen Han-chung, analyst for Yungli Securities.
"This downward correction is not driven by any fundamental factors on the economy," Chen said.
Losses were spread evenly across all major sectors. Electronics, the sector widely seen as boasting the island's best short-term outlook, fell 2.02 percent.
Accton Technology plunged by the daily seven-percent limit or T$7 to close at T$93.50. Primax Electronics also finished limit-down, dropping T$6 to T$80.50.
Electronics had risen earlier in the session on hopes that many of the listed integrated circuits-related firms may receive big orders from U.S. chipmaker Intel Corp.
"But the expectation was not enough to fend off profit-taking," Chen said.
Profit-taking also eroded gains for IC foundry maker Taiwan Semiconductor. It closed up a scant 50 cents at T$94 after earlier rising to a high of T$98.
Brokers said they expected the correction to continue in the near term. A 8,420-8,520 range was seen for Friday.
Taiwan's financial markets are closed on Thursday due to a bank holiday.
